items.expl: Repair Café teaches people to fix household objects.

groups.title: A useful mistake
groups.passage:
Luca had promised to bake bread for his flatmates, although he had never used the new oven. He read the recipe twice, mixed the ingredients and put the dough in the oven. Ten minutes later, he noticed that he had forgotten the yeast. The bread was flat and hard.

Instead of throwing it away, Luca cut it into thin pieces and toasted them with garlic and herbs. His flatmates liked the crunchy result more than ordinary bread. They suggested calling it Luca's toast. Luca still wanted to bake proper bread, so he wrote “yeast” at the top of his shopping list. He learned that a mistake can become useful when you stop and look at it differently.

items.stem: What had Luca never used before?
items.expl: Luca had never used the new oven.
The passage says Luca forgot the yeast.

items.stem: What did Luca make from the bread?
items.expl: He toasted thin pieces with garlic and herbs.

items.stem: How did Luca's flatmates feel about the result?
items.expl: They liked the crunchy result more than ordinary bread.
opts: They preferred it to ordinary bread.

items.stem: What did Luca put on his shopping list?
items.expl: He wrote yeast at the top of his list for next time.

groups.title: A day at the lake
groups.passage:
Our class arrived at the lake before the other visitors. The guide showed us a map and explained that the eastern path was closed. We followed the western path, which passed a small bird-watching shelter.

At midday we ate beside the water. Afterwards, dark clouds appeared, so the guide changed the plan. We returned to the visitor centre rather than climbing the hill. The rain began while we were inside, and we spent the afternoon looking at photographs of local wildlife.

items.expl: The guide explained that the eastern path was closed.
It passed a small shelter for watching birds.

items.stem: Why did the guide change the afternoon plan?
items.expl: Dark clouds suggested that rain was coming.

items.stem: Where did the class go instead of climbing the hill?
items.expl: They returned to the visitor centre.

items.stem: What did the class do in the afternoon?
items.expl: They looked at photographs while the rain fell.

groups.title: A new neighbour
groups.passage: When Hana moved into the apartment, her neighbour offered to (1) ___ her the best places to shop. Hana was pleased (2) ___ the building was close to a market. On Saturday, they walked there (3) ___ . The market was busier (4) ___ Hana expected, but she found everything she needed. Her neighbour also explained which stalls sold food (5) ___ local farms. Hana decided to return the following week, (6) ___ she wanted to try the fresh bread.

items.expl: The structure is “offered to show her”.
Because gives the reason Hana was pleased.
The phrase is “walked to the market”.
The comparative form uses “busier than”.
Food comes from local farms.
Because explains why Hana will return.

groups.title: Message about a walk
groups.passage:
Hi Jo,

Are you free (1) ___ Saturday? I am planning a walk through the hills. We can meet (2) ___ the café at nine. The path is not difficult, but bring a coat (3) ___ the weather may turn cold. I have checked the map (4) ___ I will carry a first-aid kit. We should be home (5) ___ sunset. Please tell (6) ___ if you can come.

Mara

items.expl: A day uses the preposition “on”.
The meeting place is at the café.
Because gives the reason for bringing a coat.
And joins the two things Mara will do.
They should arrive home before sunset.
The phrase is “tell me”.

groups.title: The night market project
groups.passage:
A group of young shop owners wanted to make the town centre livelier in winter. They proposed a night market with food stalls, handmade goods and music. The council agreed, but only if the group kept the street clear for emergency vehicles.

The first market was smaller than expected because heavy rain kept some sellers away. Those who came moved their tables under a covered walkway. Visitors still enjoyed the event, and several people asked when the next one would be. The organisers learned to prepare a wet-weather plan. They now hold the market once a month and give one stall free to a local charity.

items.stem: Why did the shop owners suggest a night market?
items.expl: They wanted the town centre to be livelier in winter.
opts: To make the centre livelier in winter.

items.stem: What condition did the council make?
items.expl: The street had to stay clear for emergency vehicles.
opts: The market had to close monthly.
Every stall had to sell food.
The street had to remain clear.

items.stem: Why was the first market small?
items.expl: Heavy rain kept some sellers away.
opts: Some sellers stayed away because of rain.

items.stem: Where did some sellers put their tables?
items.expl: They moved tables under a covered walkway.

items.stem: What does the market now do for a charity?
items.expl: One stall is free to a local charity.

groups.title: A changed travel plan
groups.passage:
Maya planned to visit the island by ferry. She checked the timetable the night before and packed a small bag. At the harbour, a notice announced that the ferry would be delayed because of strong winds.

Maya considered going home, but another passenger suggested a bus to a different harbour. The bus cost more, yet it left quickly. Maya arrived on the island later than planned and missed the first museum tour. She was not disappointed for long: the second tour was smaller, and the guide answered all her questions.

items.expl: She checked it the night before travelling.
Strong winds caused the ferry delay.
The passenger suggested taking a bus to a different harbour.
She arrived too late for the first museum tour.

items.stem: Why did Maya enjoy the second tour?
items.expl: The second tour was smaller and the guide answered questions.
opts: It was smaller and allowed questions.

groups.title: Learning to swim
groups.passage: Nina had always wanted to learn to swim, but she felt (1) ___ near deep water. Her instructor began (2) ___ simple breathing exercises in the shallow end. Nina practised every week and gradually became (3) ___ confident. The instructor also taught her how to stay calm (4) ___ she swallowed water. After three months, Nina could swim across the pool (5) ___ stopping. She was proud of the progress she had (6) ___.

items.expl: Nervous means worried or afraid near deep water.
The instructor began with simple exercises.
“More confident” shows gradual improvement.
When introduces the situation of swallowing water.
The phrase is “without stopping”.
The phrase is “progress she had made”.

groups.title: A message about a course
groups.passage:
Hi Ben,

I have joined a cooking course (1) ___ the community centre. It takes place (2) ___ Wednesday evenings and finishes at nine. We learn how (3) ___ prepare a different dish each week. Last night we cooked soup, (4) ___ everyone enjoyed. The teacher says we can bring a friend (5) ___ we tell her first. Would you like to come (6) ___ week?

Eva

items.expl: The course is at the community centre.
An evening on a named day uses “on”.
The structure is “learn how to prepare”.
Which refers to the soup and joins the relative clause.
If introduces the condition for bringing a friend.
The phrase is “next week”.

groups.title: A letter from the coast
groups.passage:
Dear Sam,

I arrived in Port Ellis last week to work at an aquarium. I expected the town to be quiet, but there is more to do than I imagined. Every morning I help feed the seals, and twice a week I give visitors a short talk about plastic in the sea.

My flat is small but bright. It is above a shop that sells fishing equipment, so I sometimes hear deliveries before breakfast. At weekends I walk along the harbour. The best part is the old lighthouse, which is open to visitors on Saturdays. You should come in August; the aquarium is planning a night event then.

Best wishes,
Tariq

items.expl: Tariq works at the aquarium.

items.stem: What does Tariq talk to visitors about?
items.expl: His talks explain the problem of plastic in the sea.

items.stem: Why does Tariq sometimes wake early?
items.expl: Deliveries to the shop below can be heard before breakfast.

items.stem: When can visitors enter the old lighthouse?
items.expl: The lighthouse is open to visitors on Saturdays.

items.stem: What will happen at the aquarium in August?
items.expl: The aquarium is planning a night event.

groups.title: The forgotten umbrella
groups.passage:
After leaving the cinema, Rosa noticed that rain had started. She opened her umbrella, but the handle broke. A stranger offered her a place under his large umbrella until they reached the bus stop.

Rosa thanked him and took the bus home. The next day she returned to the cinema to ask whether anyone had found her umbrella. The manager had kept it at the ticket desk. Rosa was surprised that the handle had only come loose; it could be repaired. She decided to repair it rather than buy another one.

items.stem: What happened when Rosa opened her umbrella?
items.expl: The umbrella handle broke when she opened it.

items.stem: Who helped Rosa reach the bus stop?
items.expl: A stranger shared a large umbrella with her.

items.stem: Where was the umbrella the next day?
items.expl: The cinema manager had kept it at the ticket desk.
She discovered that the handle was loose rather than permanently broken.

items.stem: What did Rosa decide to do?
items.expl: She chose to repair it instead of buying another.

groups.title: A helpful neighbour
groups.passage: When my washing machine stopped working, I asked my neighbour whether he could (1) ___ me a hand. He arrived with a small box of tools and quickly found the (2) ___ . A coin had become stuck in the filter. He removed it, (3) ___ the machine worked again. I wanted to pay him, (4) ___ he refused. Instead, he asked me to water his plants (5) ___ he was away. I was happy to help, because he had saved me the cost of (6) ___ a repair service.

items.expl: The expression is “give me a hand”.
A stuck coin was the problem.
So shows the result: the machine worked again.
But contrasts the offer with the refusal.
While describes the time he was away.
The phrase is “the cost of calling a service”.

groups.title: A sports day note
groups.passage:
Dear team,

Sports day is next Friday, and we need to meet (1) ___ the field at eight. Please wear shoes (2) ___ are comfortable for running. The school will provide water, (3) ___ bring a hat if the sun is strong. Our first event begins (4) ___ half past eight. I will keep the list of names, so tell (5) ___ if you change your event. We should finish (6) ___ lunchtime.

Ms Lee

items.expl: The team meets on the field.
That introduces the relative clause describing the shoes.
So introduces advice based on strong sun.
A clock time uses “at”.
The phrase is “tell me”.
The event should finish before lunchtime.
